extracted.intended_audience: comparative psychologists, anthropologists, students and researchers of human mental evolution
extracted.subtask_description: A proposed programme for comparative psychology of man: enumerates the mental traits, dimensions, and subordinate inquiries by which differences between races, sexes, and social types should be studied. Meant to guide empirical and theoretical investigations into human mental evolution and its social relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate of mental development
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the inferior human races may be expected to complete their mental evolution sooner than members of the superior races; travellers comment on precocity and early arrest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether this contrast is consistent across all racial groups; subordinate inquiries: (a) sex differences in rate and degree of development; (b) relation between period of arrest and period of puberty; (c) whether rapid evolution implies proportionally early mental decay; (d) whether the whole cycle of mental changes (ascending, uniform, descending) is compressed into a shorter interval in lower types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative plasticity (mental modifiability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of mental modifiability which remains in adult life, and its relation to mental mass, complexity, and rapidity of evolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare across animal kingdom and human races: lower, reflex-guided organisms show less changeability; as nervous structure complicates, individual experience shapes conduct more. Examine relation of plasticity to precocity, early completion of mental development, and to social state (how social conditions determine and react on plasticity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Variability (short-term inconstancy vs long-term unchangeableness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish minute-to-minute inconstancy of manifestations from average unchangeableness over long periods; these traits may co-exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study how far variability characterizes whole minds versus specific parts. Examples: infants with rapid changes but overall fixed character; 'inferior' races showing great rigidity of general character with irregular passing manifestations—measure intellectual and emotional persistence (attention span, endurance of feelings) and qualifications to broad statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impulsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency to sudden, brief, often violent emotional outbursts which sway conduct without consistency; allied to lack of persistence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine connections with degree of mental evolution and reflex-like nervous processes. Sub-questions: (a) relation to other traits besides mental evolution (e.g., New-World vs Old-World differences, link to constitutional vivacity); (b) relation to social state—how social union checks impulsiveness; (c) what feelings fostered by social state (fear of others, social instinct, desire to accumulate property, sympathy, sentiment of justice) contribute to checking impulsiveness and in what order/degree/combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of racial mixture on mental nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the union of divergent human varieties is mentally injurious (if extremely unlike) or beneficial (if slightly divergent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate historical and demographic evidence (examples given: descendants of refugees producing notable men) to determine if mixture produces more plastic, impressible natures that foster originality and adaptation. Ask how conquest and subsequent mixture have aided civilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of difference between the sexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether mental unlikeness of males and females is constant across types of mankind or variable, and if variable, under what conditions and to what amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare across races (e.g., bearded vs beardless races) to discern variability in sexual mental differences and the conditions that influence them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference in mental mass and complexity between sexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative mental mass and relative mental complexity of men and women considered in relation to reproductive cost and other physiological and social factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study connections with reproductive ages and durations, and how habits of food and physical exertion (e.g., brutality, excess labour, defective nutrition) may cause arrest of mental development in one sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variation of sexual differences (sex-limited heredity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether mental natures of the sexes in divergent types of man have diverged in unlike ways and degrees, implying transmission of accumulated differences to descendants of the same sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider heredity limited by sex as applied to cerebral structures as well as other bodily structures; test whether divergences occur across races and societies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes of sexual differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Relations between variable sexual differences and the different parts the sexes play in life; cumulative effects of habit on function and structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether persistent differences in activities between sexes across generations produce sexual adaptations of mind; include cases where social/domestic role inversions produce inverted mental differences (e.g., Khasi Hill-tribes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental modifiability in the two sexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative plasticity of men and women within each race; question whether women are less modifiable than men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe conservatism of women (adhesion to established ideas and practices) across civilized, semi-civilized, and uncivilized societies; include ethnographic examples (e.g., Juangs) and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: The sexual sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Amounts and characters of the higher feelings arising from relations of the sexes, and their development with civilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subordinate inquiries: (a) dependence on intellectual advance and growth of imaginative power; (b) relation to emotional advance and evolution of sympathy; (c) relations to polyandry and polygyny; (d) tendency toward and fostering by monogamy; relation to family bond and child-rearing quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency to mimic motions and sounds of others — often almost involuntary and 'meaningless' repetition — stronger in lower types and decreasing with self-regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study automatic mimicry and its relation to less automatic mimicry exhibited in persistent customs. Consider its dual role: aiding social fixity necessary for survival, yet hindering desirable social change. Examine how decrease of irrational mimicry correlates with stages of social life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incuriosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of rational curiosity about unfamiliar civilized products among the lowest races, in contrast to partially-civilized peoples who show rational curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research the relation of incuriosity to intellectual nature, emotional nature, and social state; avoid projecting one's own reactions onto others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Vague heading covering: degree of generality, abstractness, definiteness, coherence of ideas; and possession of notions of class, cause, uniformity, law, truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop tests for stages of development: (a) analyze successive stages independently; (b) examine connections with cooperative intellectual conceptions; (c) relate to progress of language, arts, and social organization. Use linguistic phenomena systematically: number and degrees of general and abstract words in a people's vocabulary and their orders/grades to yield evidence of intellectual stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peculiar aptitudes (specialities of intelligence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special abilities related to modes of life and adaptation — e.g., skill in weapons, powers of tracking, quick discrimination, and race-peculiar aesthetic aptitudes (pictorial representation, musical faculty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and analyze such specialties, note anomalies (e.g., low-grade groups capable of faithful animal representation; other races scarcely recognizing pictorial representations), and search for causes of race-peculiar aptitudes (including musical examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialities of emotional nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct emotional traits that vary by race and relate intimately to social phenomena and social progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key traits to observe include: (a) gregariousness/sociality — degree of desire for fellow-presence; (b) intolerance of restraint — governability vs admiration for authority; (c) desire for praise — strength and connection to social restraints; (d) acquisitive propensity — desire for property and its relation to forms of property (tribal, family, individual) and social development. Study interactions between sentiments and social state.

rubrics_metrics.name: The altruistic sentiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Highest sentiments arising from sympathy — their evolution with civilization and reciprocal influence with social organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange comparisons under three heads: (a) pity — observe toward offspring, sick/aged, enemies; (b) generosity — distinct from love of display; observe giving, relinquishment of pleasures, active efforts, range (relatives, same society, other societies), and whether actions are impulsive or provident; (c) justice — measure in regard to lives, freedom, property, and minor claims. Always compare these sentiments alongside social states (forms of government, laws, class relations) since they largely determine them.
